chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Abdullah ibn Talha, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The fasting person is in a state of worship, even if he is on his bed, as long as he does not backbite a Muslim.'

key_terms.الصائم: Al-Sa'im — the one who fasts; the practitioner of sawm (fasting)
key_terms.عبادة: 'Ibadah — worship, devotion, a state of being in service to God
key_terms.فراش: Firash — bed, sleeping place; used here to indicate rest or inactivity
key_terms.مسلم: Muslim — a fellow believer; the prohibition applies to speaking ill of any Muslim
key_terms.يغتب: Yaghtatib — to backbite, to speak ill of someone in their absence; ghibah

ai.seo_question: Is a fasting person always in a state of worship according to hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) transmits this saying of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) that the fasting person maintains a continuous state of divine worship throughout their day of fasting — even while resting — provided they do not engage in backbiting (ghibah) against a fellow Muslim. This hadith links the spiritual reward of fasting to the avoidance of harmful speech, teaching that fasting is not merely abstention from food and drink but encompasses protection of other Muslims' honor. For the early Muslim audience, this was a profound reminder that acts of worship can be nullified or diminished by moral transgressions.
